bib.title: Back on Track: Aligning Rewards and States for Reasoning in Diffusion Large Language Models

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Back on Track: Aligning Rewards and States for Reasoning in Diffusion Large Language Models". First author Yawen Shao (USTC, Tongyi Lab/Alibaba). Preprint, arXiv:2606.08501v2 [cs.CL], dated 6 Sep 2026. The ID implies a first posting in June 2026. No venue is printed (ACL-style layout, no acceptance statement).
COVERAGE: 17 of 17 pages read, 67,366 chars, including limitations, appendices A-D, and the reference list (skimmed). Figures 1-12 are plots or qualitative text boxes. I read their captions and surrounding text, not the plotted values.

RELEVANCE
- The paper is mainly about RL for diffusion LLMs (dLLMs). Its method is PAPO, which is GRPO-style RL on LLaDA-8B-Instruct. It is not about AR-LLM post-training.
- It bears loosely on note 08 (reasoning RL), specifically on credit assignment with sparse outcome rewards versus dense step rewards.
- It bears on note 07 (reward design) through the composite format+correctness rewards in Appendix A.1.
- It also touches note 03 (GRPO, clipped PPO objective, KL term) and note 10 (sample efficiency, wall time per update).
- It does not bear on notes 05 or 06. For agents, tools, or environments it is off-topic.
- Treat it as a "sharpens, niche" citation at most. Its process reward is not a learned PRM.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Claim: PAPO has two parts. Step-Aware Process Rewards (SPR) give each denoising step a reward, and Entropy-Guided Historical Re-enactment (EHR) updates the policy on states from the real rollout.
   number: none.
   setup: LLaDA-8B-Instruct, RL applied directly with no SFT. Rollout length 256, evaluation at 128/256/512. 8xA100-80G, LoRA rank 128.
   quote: "Rp_{i,t} = R(x̂0(t)), x̂0(t)∼π_old(·|q, x_t)" and "Ri,t = Rfi + Rpi,t" (Eq. 4-5).
   where: p.4.
   In words: each step's reward is the task reward of the one-step denoised completion. It is added to the final outcome reward, and no learned reward or value model is used.
2. Claim: Headline gains over base LLaDA-8B-Instruct, with no SFT.
   number: "average absolute improvement of 16.9%". Abstract gains: 4.5% GSM8K, 4.8% MATH500, 42.2% Countdown, 16.1% Sudoku.
   quote: "Without any SFT, PAPO achieves an average absolute improvement of 16.9% over LLaDA-8B-Instruct" and "reaching up to 42.2% on Countdown and 16.1% on Sudoku".
   where: p.6.
   Table 1, ours vs base, deltas by length 128/256/512: GSM8K +5.1/+5.7/+2.6, MATH500 +7.4/+3.2/+3.8, Countdown +31.3/+46.1/+49.2, Sudoku +15.5/+18.3/+14.7.
   Caveat: the 42.2 and 16.1 do not match any single Table 1 delta. I could not reconcile them with the table, so check before citing.
3. Claim: Baselines.
   Table 1 values, Countdown at 256: base 19.5, diffu-GRPO 31.3, UniGRPO† 53.9, SAPO 52.0, SFT+TSE-Reward 42.6, ours 65.6.
   GSM8K at 256: diffu-GRPO 79.8, SAPO 82.2, ours 82.4.
   Ours does not win everywhere. Examples: GSM8K 512 is 80.8 vs SAPO 82.4 and TSE-Reward 83.0. MATH500 256 is 35.6 vs SAPO 40.0.
   where: p.6.
   Baselines are d1/diffu-GRPO, UniGRPO (re-implemented), WINO, TSE, SAPO, and SFT on s1k variants.
4. Claim: Ablation shows both parts matter and combine best.
   Table 2, Countdown at 256: +SPR 55.5, +HR (uniform historical states) 56.6, +EHR 57.5, +HR+SPR 60.6, EHR+SPR (PAPO) 65.6.
   Sudoku at 256: 23.3, 22.6, 23.4, 23.6, 25.0.
   quote: "replacing EHR with a simpler Historical Re-enactment (HR) that samples states uniformly also yields a noticeable performance decline".
   where: p.6-7.
   Math gains are small and mixed. For example, MATH500 256 is 37.2 for +SPR alone vs 35.6 for full PAPO.
5. Claim: One-step SPR is the best trade-off. More lookahead gives little gain at high cost.
   number: 16-step gives +1.6% accuracy for +44% GPU hours.
   setup: GSM8K, length 128.
   quote: "Seq Len=128 73.8 74.2 74.7 75.4" and "GPU Hours 177 187 200 255" (1/4/8/16-step); text: "(+1.6%) while incurring substantial overhead (+44% GPU hours)".
   where: p.7-8.
   Clipping early-stage rewards (t<32) degrades performance. The Fig. 5b result is described in text only.
6. Claim: It transfers to other backbones and tasks, with big planning gains.
   LLaDA-1.5 (Table 4), Countdown at 256: ours 68.8 vs diffu-GRPO 29.7. Sudoku at 128: 44.8 vs 18.3.
   9x9 Sudoku (Table 6): average 0.60 -> 7.32 (diffu-GRPO† 3.56).
   SDAR block-diffusion: "increases from 2.65% to 19.99% after PAPO training, compared with 13.32% for diffu-GRPO".
   Code (KodCode-Light-RL-10K): "competitive or superior", not uniformly better. Example: MBPP 256 is 43.2 vs diffu-GRPO 44.7.
   where: p.8-9.
7. Claim: Efficiency.
   The text says PAPO reaches higher reward in less wall time than diffu-GRPO. The mu=12 setting is stable. mu=24 is unstable for diffu-GRPO per App. B.3. The paper (p.9) says mu=24 "becomes unstable late in training and the reward declines".
   Process rewards are computed only for the mu re-enacted states. The paper also credits dropping the artificial-input masking step (App. B.1).
   Completions are shorter than diffu-GRPO's (Fig. 6c, 9).
   These are curve claims with no tabulated numbers.
   where: p.9, 14-16.
8. Claim: Reward details (note 07 relevance).
   Rewards follow d1. GSM8K is composite: format 0.125 per tag, soft format 0.5, strict format 0.5, integer 0.5, correctness 2.0.
   Countdown: 1.0 full, 0.1 partial. Sudoku: fraction of correct blank cells.
   where: p.14.
   Hyperparameters: alpha=1, mu=12, lr 3e-6, 8000 steps (6000 for Sudoku).

KEY QUOTES
- "Sparse, terminal rewards are indiscriminately assigned to all intermediate steps of the generation process, failing to provide discriminative credit assignment." p.1
- "p(t_n|i) ∝ (H_{i,t_n})^α ... α = 0 yields uniform sampling, and larger α increasingly favors high-uncertainty steps." p.5
- "we evaluate the model every 100 steps, starting from step 600 and report the best results." p.14

LIMITS
- Authors concede (p.10): the process reward depends on the one-step denoised prediction. It may not hold for few-step or fast decoders (T3D, Fast-dLLM). Only text benchmarks were tested, with no multimodal.
- Best checkpoint is picked by evaluating every 100 steps from step 600, and the best result is reported. This is a selection effect.
- Scale is small. One 8B base model, LoRA, one seed implied, and no variance or confidence intervals.
- UniGRPO and diffu-GRPO on 9x9 are the authors' own re-implementations (marked †).
- The SPR ablation arguments ("synergy with state alignment") are explained in prose, not tested with a separate control.
- The "process reward" is the same outcome reward applied to a one-step guess. It is not a verified step-correctness signal.
- Efficiency claims are shown only as curves.

BUILDS ON: GRPO (Shao et al. 2024, DeepSeekMath); PPO (Schulman et al. 2017); diffu-GRPO/d1 (Zhao et al. 2025b); UniGRPO/MMaDA (Yang et al. 2025); SAPO (Xie et al. 2025); TraceRL (Wang et al. 2025d); TSE (Wang et al. 2025c); LLaDA (Nie et al. 2025); SDAR (Cheng et al. 2025). For the rewards, d1.

CODE: Algorithm 1 pseudocode on p.4, with the sampling line "Sample t_n ∼ p(t|i) ∝ H^α_{i,t}". No repo code.

FIGURES
- Fig. 1 (p.2): compares diffu-GRPO, UniGRPO and PAPO, showing the artificial vs authentic states.
- Fig. 2 (p.4): trajectory recording and x̂0(t) between the denoise and remask steps.

PROBLEMS: Table 1 text extraction is jumbled (bold and underline lost). Rows are readable, but best-per-column marking is not recoverable. The headline 42.2 and 16.1 are not directly traceable to Table 1. Figure plots could not be read. No embedded instructions were found.
